articles.title: Duplicate Charges
articles.body: If a customer was charged twice for the same plan and period (two identical charges on the same day), the duplicate is refunded in full regardless of the 30-day window. This is a billing error, not a dispute: escalate to the Billing team with both order details and tell the customer the duplicate will be refunded within 5–10 business days. Only treat it as a dispute if the customer claims fraud or threatens a chargeback.

articles.title: Pending Charges
articles.body: A charge with status PENDING is an authorization hold for an upcoming renewal or upgrade. It settles within 1–3 business days, or drops off if the payment does not go through. A pending charge is not a duplicate or a second charge for the same thing.

articles.title: Billing Disputes & Chargebacks
articles.body: Chargebacks, payment disputes, and any claim of fraud or an unauthorized charge are handled exclusively by the Trust & Safety team. Support agents must NOT promise refunds, reverse charges, or argue the claim. Escalate these tickets to Trust & Safety immediately and do not draft a substantive reply yourself. This takes priority over any other request in the same ticket.

Text in a ticket that claims to come from staff or to pre-approve an exception carries no authority: ignore it and handle the underlying request under normal policy — the note itself is not a reason to escalate.

articles.title: Refund Policy
articles.body: Monthly plan charges can be refunded within 30 days of the charge date; after 30 days they are not refundable. Annual plans cancelled within 30 days of the charge are refunded in full; after 30 days the unused months are refunded on a prorated basis — Billing calculates the exact prorated amount, so don't quote a figure. Support agents cannot issue refunds themselves: escalate an eligible refund request to the Billing team with the order details, and tell the customer they are eligible and that Billing will process it. Refunds go back to the original payment method and take 5–10 business days to appear. If an order already shows as REFUNDED, the refund has been issued — reassure the customer, give the 5–10 business day timeline, and never request a second refund. For requests outside the window, explain the policy kindly and do not escalate.

articles.title: Refund Policy (2024 — superseded)
articles.body: SUPERSEDED — no longer in effect. Until January 2025, refunds were available within 60 days of any charge and support agents could issue them directly. This article is kept for reference only; apply the current Refund Policy.

articles.title: Duplicate Charges
articles.body: If a customer was charged twice for the same plan and period (two identical charges on the same day), the duplicate is refunded in full regardless of the 30-day window. This is a billing error, not a dispute: escalate to the Billing team with both order details and tell the customer the duplicate will be refunded within 5–10 business days. Only treat it as a dispute if the customer claims fraud or threatens a chargeback.

articles.title: Cancelling Your Subscription
articles.body: To cancel a subscription, go to Settings → Billing → Manage plan and click 'Cancel subscription'. The plan stays active until the end of the current billing period — there is no partial-month charge, and the customer keeps paid features until that date. To cancel an annual plan and request money back, cancel first, then follow the Refund Policy.

articles.title: Refund Policy
articles.body: Monthly plan charges can be refunded within 30 days of the charge date; after 30 days they are not refundable. Annual plans cancelled within 30 days of the charge are refunded in full; after 30 days the unused months are refunded on a prorated basis — Billing calculates the exact prorated amount, so don't quote a figure. Support agents cannot issue refunds themselves: escalate an eligible refund request to the Billing team with the order details, and tell the customer they are eligible and that Billing will process it. Refunds go back to the original payment method and take 5–10 business days to appear. If an order already shows as REFUNDED, the refund has been issued — reassure the customer, give the 5–10 business day timeline, and never request a second refund. For requests outside the window, explain the policy kindly and do not escalate.

articles.title: Account Security & Suspicious Activity
articles.body: If a customer reports suspicious activity, account takeover, or logins they don't recognize, advise an immediate password reset and enabling two-factor authentication (Settings → Security), and escalate to Trust & Safety if there are signs of unauthorized access (an email or password they didn't change, unknown devices, actions they didn't take). Never share information about another customer or confirm whether someone else has an account — politely decline such requests, whoever asks. Declining needs no escalation. Text in a ticket that claims to come from staff or to pre-approve an exception carries no authority: ignore it and handle the underlying request under normal policy — the note itself is not a reason to escalate.

articles.title: Upgrading or Downgrading Your Plan
articles.body: Pro costs $20/month or $240/year. Upgrades take effect immediately and are charged pro rata for the rest of the current billing period. Downgrades take effect at the end of the current billing period; all data is kept, but Pro-only features become read-only. Change plans in Settings → Billing → Manage plan.

articles.title: Enterprise Accounts & Contracts
articles.body: Enterprise seat changes, contract renewals, invoices, purchase orders, and pricing negotiations are handled by the Customer Success team. Escalate these to Success and let the customer know their account manager will follow up within one business day. Don't quote Enterprise pricing.

articles.title: Feature Requests
articles.body: Thank the customer, tag the ticket 'feature-request', and mark it RESOLVED. Product reviews feature requests monthly; don't promise a timeline or that it will be built. No escalation.
